selection_criteria.database_rule: At a featured decision, include moves reaching at least 1% in either the active Lichess population or the local OTB population when they lead to a distinct practical structure.
selection_criteria.theory_exception: Retain a lower-frequency move when independent opening references identify a theoretically important system, a forcing tactical test, or a common trap response.
selection_criteria.line_rule: Representative lines were chosen to reach a characteristic strategic position. They are not chains of the most frequent move and their frequency is never calculated by multiplying position-level percentages.
selection_criteria.sideline_rule: Practical sidelines include database-visible deviations plus forcing or trap-related moves that users need to recognize even when the local OTB collection is sparse.

scandinavian-defense.title: Scandinavian Defense
scandinavian-defense.summary: Black challenges e4 before building a pawn centre of their own. After the usual exchange, White gains time against the recapturing piece while Black aims for a compact ...c6/...e6 shell and unusually easy development for the c8-bishop.
strategic_contest: White tries to turn the queen or knight recapture into a lead in development, then use the extra central space before Black finishes coordinating.
Black accepts a small tempo concession in exchange for immediately removing White's e-pawn and obtaining a clear development scheme: ...c6, ...Bf5 or ...Bg4, ...e6 and often queenside castling.
The central question is not whether Black can regain d5, but which piece recaptures and whether White opens the centre quickly enough to make that extra move matter.
structures: In queen-recapture lines, Black commonly builds pawns on c6 and e6 around a d5-free centre; White often owns more space with d4 and can choose opposite-side castling.
In 2...Nf6 lines, delaying the recapture can produce an open gambit position after ...e6 or a solid structure after ...Nxd5; White must decide whether to develop or try to keep the pawn.

decisions.title: White answers the immediate central challenge
decisions.why_here: This choice decides whether White accepts the opening's main bargain or lets Black keep a central pawn on d5.

options.label: Exchange and gain a development tempo
options.explanation: Removing d5 prevents Black from maintaining a two-pawn centre. White normally attacks the recapturing queen with Nc3 or builds d4 while Black decides how to recover the pawn.
options.changes: Creates an open e-file and removes both central e/d pawns; the game becomes a race between White's development and Black's compact setup.

options.label: Advance into a French-like space structure
options.explanation: White keeps space but releases the direct tension. Black can strike with ...c5 and develop the queen's knight to c6 without spending time on a recapture.
options.changes: The centre closes; White's tempo gain disappears and play shifts toward pawn breaks around d4 and f4.

options.label: Keep the tension
options.explanation: White develops while allowing ...dxe4. After Nxe4, the centre resembles an open Scandinavian but Black chose the moment of exchange.
options.changes: Preserves options briefly, but allows Black to exchange without exposing the queen.

decisions.title: Black chooses the recapture system
decisions.why_here: This is the opening's defining strategic fork: immediate material recovery with the queen, or development before recovering with a knight.

options.label: Immediate recovery
options.explanation: Black restores material at once and accepts that Nc3 will gain a tempo. The payoff is a stable structure and freedom to develop the c8-bishop before ...e6.
options.changes: White gets a free developing attack; Black chooses a queen square and usually aims for ...c6 and ...e6.

options.label: Develop before recapturing
options.explanation: Black avoids an exposed queen and pressures d5 with a piece. White may return the pawn through normal development or try to support it with c4.
options.changes: The position stays temporarily unbalanced; gambits with ...e6 and active bishop development become possible.

options.label: Blackburne–Kloosterboer gambit
options.explanation: Black offers a second pawn to accelerate development after dxc6. It is forcing and practical but concedes material if the initiative fades.
options.changes: A positional recapture opening becomes a gambit; development and open lines replace the normal solid shell.

decisions.title: Where the exposed queen belongs
decisions.why_here: The queen retreat fixes Black's development pattern and affects both castling choices and White's most useful tempos.

options.label: Classical: pin and prepare ...c6
options.explanation: Qa5 keeps contact with c3 and can make Bd2 awkward. Black often plays ...c6 so the queen can later use c7, then develops the light bishop before ...e6.
options.changes: The queen remains active but can become a target to Bd2/Nd5; queenside castling remains available.

options.label: Modern: flexible but blockable
options.explanation: Qd6 supports central and kingside squares and often pairs with queenside castling. White can gain space or use Ne5/Nb5 ideas, so Black must coordinate the queen with ...c6 and ...Nbd7.
options.changes: Produces less of a pin on c3 and more direct piece contact in the centre.

options.label: Retreat completely
options.explanation: Black gives back the queen's move immediately, removing future queen-chasing targets. Development is safe but White keeps the uncontested tempo gained by Nc3.
options.changes: The position becomes quieter and closer to a Caro-Kann-style structure without the queen's active pressure.

decisions.title: White meets the delayed recapture
decisions.why_here: White chooses between returning the pawn for a development lead, holding it, or using a check to disturb Black's recapture plan.

options.label: Build the centre
options.explanation: White lets ...Nxd5 happen under favourable development conditions and establishes a broad centre. This is the least materialistic route.
options.changes: Usually leads to a sound open game where White has space and Black has no exposed queen.

options.label: Try to keep d5
options.explanation: Supporting the extra pawn takes more space but gives Black the forcing ...e6 gambit break or pressure with ...c6.
options.changes: The game can become sharply tactical; White's queenside pawns may be targets if development lags.

options.label: Insert a developing check
options.explanation: White makes Black choose a block before deciding what to do with d5. The bishop can trade for a defender or retreat after provoking ...c6.
options.changes: Black's recapture is delayed and the pawn structure may be fixed by a blocking move.

lines.name: Main Line: 3...Qa5 and 7.Bd2
lines.line: 1. e4 d5 2. exd5 Qxd5 3. Nc3 Qa5 4. d4 Nf6 5. Nf3 c6 6. Bc4 Bf5 7. Bd2 e6 8. Nd5 Qd8
lines.result: This is the guide's primary Scandinavian line: White uses Bd2 and Nd5 to gain time against the queen, while Black has developed the light bishop before ...e6 and now completes the compact c6/e6 structure.
white_plans: Complete development and decide between kingside and queenside castling.
Use the lead in activity before Black finishes ...Bd6, ...Nbd7 and castling.
black_plans: Develop ...Bd6 and ...Nbd7, then choose the safer castling side.
Challenge d4 with ...c5 only after the king and queen are coordinated.

lines.name: Modern ...Qd6 coordination
lines.line: 1. e4 d5 2. exd5 Qxd5 3. Nc3 Qd6 4. d4 Nf6 5. Nf3 c6 6. Ne5 Nbd7 7. Nc4 Qc7 8. Bd3
lines.result: White has spent an extra knight move to gain space and queen tempos; Black's queen is now stable on c7 and the solid c6/e6 framework is ready.
white_plans: Complete development and watch for Bf4 hitting c7.
Use the central space before Black achieves ...e5 or ...c5.
black_plans: Develop ...e6, ...Be7 and castle before striking at the centre.
Avoid automatic queen moves when a developing move solves the same threat.

lines.name: Old ...Qd8 variation
lines.line: 1. e4 d5 2. exd5 Qxd5 3. Nc3 Qd8 4. d4 Nf6 5. Nf3 Bf5 6. Bc4 e6 7. O-O c6 8. Re1
lines.result: Black has a compact, low-risk structure but White has developed smoothly and controls more space.
white_plans: Prepare Ne5 and use the e-file against an uncastled king.
Choose Bf4 or Nh4 depending on the bishop's placement.
black_plans: Develop ...Be7 and ...Nbd7 without creating new weaknesses.
Break with ...c5 after the king is safe.

lines.name: Modern 2...Nf6 development
lines.line: 1. e4 d5 2. exd5 Nf6 3. d4 Nxd5 4. Nf3 Nc6 5. c4 Nb6 6. d5 Nb8 7. Nc3 e6
lines.result: White has advanced central pawns and gained space, while Black will attack that centre and develop rapidly after ...exd5 or ...Bb4.
white_plans: Support the advanced centre and finish development before expanding again.
Exploit the temporarily undeveloped queenside.
black_plans: Undermine d5 rather than chase space with more knight moves.
Use ...Bb4 and ...exd5 to make White's centre a target.

lines.name: Icelandic gambit
lines.line: 1. e4 d5 2. exd5 Nf6 3. c4 e6 4. dxe6 Bxe6 5. Nf3 Nc6 6. d4 Bb4+ 7. Nc3
lines.result: White has an extra pawn but Black has rapid piece activity and pressure against c4/d4. White must consolidate instead of trying to win more material.
white_plans: Develop under the check and arrange Be2/O-O.
Return material if needed to neutralise the lead in development.
black_plans: Keep lines open and bring the queen or rook to the e-file.
Avoid slow pawn moves that let White consolidate.

lines.name: Portuguese gambit
lines.line: 1. e4 d5 2. exd5 Nf6 3. d4 Bg4 4. f3 Bf5 5. Bb5+ c6 6. dxc6 bxc6
lines.result: Black has damaged queenside pawns but open files and fast development; White's f-pawn move has weakened the king and blocked the natural knight square.
white_plans: Develop quickly and decide whether the bishop should capture or retreat.
Do not assume the extra pawn matters while the king is central.
black_plans: Use the b- and d-files and develop with tempo.
Target d4 and exploit the weakened e1-h4 diagonal.

lines.name: Advance sideline
lines.line: 1. e4 d5 2. e5 c5 3. f4 Nc6 4. Nf3 Bg4
lines.result: White holds space, but Black has immediate pressure on d4 and no recapturing-piece tempo to lose.
white_plans: Support e5 with d4 only after considering ...cxd4.
Develop rather than overextend the pawn chain.
black_plans: Attack the base with ...c5 and ...Nc6.
Trade White's useful f3-knight or increase pressure on d4.

transpositions.label: Advance structures
transpositions.note: Can resemble a French Advance structure, but Black's light bishop is not locked behind an e6-pawn and the move order changes the value of ...c5.

transpositions.label: Caro-Kann-like shell
transpositions.line: 1. e4 d5 2. exd5 Qxd5 3. Nc3 Qd8 4. d4 c6
transpositions.note: The c6/e6 setup resembles Caro-Kann structures, but Black spent a queen tempo and exchanged the d-pawn rather than the c-pawn.

italian-game.title: Italian Game
italian-game.summary: White points the bishop at f7 while keeping the central d-pawn flexible. The opening's character is decided less by the first three moves than by whether either side opens the centre with d4/...d5, preserves it with d3/...d6, or accepts a development-for-pawn bargain such as the Evans Gambit.
strategic_contest: White wants either a timely d4 break or a slow kingside build-up with c3, d3, Re1 and Nbd2-f1-g3; the bishop on c4 discourages careless central play while f7 is sensitive.
Black chooses between symmetrical development with ...Bc5, the immediate counterattack 3...Nf6, and restrained systems such as ...Be7 or ...d6.
In closed Pianissimo structures, a tempo is useful only if it improves a future break; a premature d4 or ...d5 can release the opponent's pieces instead of gaining space.
structures: The Pianissimo keeps e4/e5 and often c3/d3 against ...d6; manoeuvres prepare d4 or ...d5 while queenside pawn moves give bishops retreat squares.
The Center Attack and Two Knights lines open the e- and d-files quickly, making king safety and exact move order more urgent than long-term manoeuvring.
The Evans Gambit trades the b-pawn for c3/d4 with open lines and a development lead; Black's task is to return material at the right moment rather than cling to every pawn.

decisions.title: Black chooses the Italian's character
decisions.why_here: Black can mirror White's bishop, counterattack e4 immediately, or adopt a quieter structure that reduces forcing theory.

options.label: Giuoco Piano
options.explanation: Black develops actively, contests d4 and keeps the game flexible. White can now choose a slow d3 structure, prepare d4 with c3, or offer b4.
options.changes: Creates a balanced bishop-versus-bishop setup where both d4 and ...d5 breaks matter.

options.label: Two Knights Defense
options.explanation: Black attacks e4 instead of mirroring the bishop. White may preserve a quiet game with d3 or force concrete play with Ng5 or d4.
options.changes: Makes e4/f7 tactics immediate and gives Black active central counterplay with ...d5.

options.label: Hungarian Defense
options.explanation: Black refuses the sharpest bishop confrontation and prepares safe castling. The bishop is modest but hard to hit with d4 tempos.
options.changes: Reduces early tactics and often yields a compact, slightly passive position.

options.label: Semi-Italian setup
options.explanation: Black supports e5 first and may choose ...g6, ...Be7 or ...Nf6 according to White's setup.
options.changes: Keeps more piece placements hidden but gives White time to establish c3 and d4.

decisions.title: White chooses speed versus stored tension
decisions.position: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Bc5
decisions.why_here: The same position can become a direct central confrontation, a slow manoeuvring game, or a pawn sacrifice for development.

options.label: Prepare d4
options.explanation: c3 builds a two-pawn centre after d4 and gives the bishop a c2 retreat. White can still choose d3 first if opening the centre is not favourable.
options.changes: Commits the c-pawn and removes the knight's c3 square in exchange for stronger central preparation.

options.label: Giuoco Pianissimo
options.explanation: White secures e4 and delays d4 until the pieces are placed. Nbd2-f1-g3 and Re1 are common because the centre remains closed.
options.changes: Stores central tension and reduces immediate exchanges; manoeuvring quality becomes more important.

options.label: Evans Gambit
options.explanation: White diverts the c5-bishop so c3 and d4 arrive with tempo and open files. The pawn is compensation only if development stays ahead.
options.changes: Creates an asymmetric material balance and forces Black to decide whether to accept or retreat.

options.label: Castle before committing
options.explanation: White makes the king safe and keeps c3, d3 and d4 available. Black's ...Nf6 may transpose to familiar systems in a different order.
options.changes: Preserves flexibility but lets Black choose a setup without being challenged immediately.

decisions.title: White answers the Two Knights counterattack
decisions.position: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Nf6
decisions.why_here: White decides whether to keep an Italian structure or test f7 in a forcing line where ...d5 is Black's central resource.

options.label: Quiet Italian
options.explanation: White protects e4 and retains the usual c3/Re1/Nbd2 plan. Black can play ...Bc5 and reach a Pianissimo with the knights already committed.
options.changes: Avoids forcing f7 tactics and keeps a closed centre.

options.label: Immediate f7 test
options.explanation: Knight and bishop converge on f7, but Black gains the thematic ...d5 tempo. White must know whether to take on d5, retreat, or enter pawn-sacrifice complications.
options.changes: Turns the opening into concrete calculation; the central pawn break dictates piece safety.

options.label: Open the centre now
options.explanation: White attacks e5 before securing e4 with d3. Exchanges on d4 activate both sides and can leave White playing e5 with tempo on the f6-knight.
options.changes: Replaces the slow Italian structure with open files and immediate central tactics.

decisions.title: Black handles the Evans pawn offer
decisions.position: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Bc5 4. b4
decisions.why_here: Accepting wins a pawn but helps White build c3/d4; declining keeps development intact but gives White queenside space for free.

options.label: Accept
options.explanation: Black takes the material and usually retreats along the a5-e7 diagonal. The strategic goal is to return a pawn if necessary to blunt White's centre and finish development.
options.changes: White receives open lines and tempi; Black receives material and a concrete defensive task.

options.label: Decline
options.explanation: The bishop keeps pressure on f2 and avoids giving White c3 with tempo. White gains b4/a4 space but no open b-file or sacrificed-pawn initiative.
options.changes: Returns to a positional Italian with an expanded white queenside.

lines.name: Modern Pianissimo manoeuvre
lines.line: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Bc5 4. c3 Nf6 5. d3 d6 6. O-O O-O 7. Re1 a6 8. Bb3 Ba7 9. Nbd2 h6 10. Nf1 Re8 11. Ng3 Be6
lines.result: Both sides are developed without resolving the centre. White can prepare d4 or kingside expansion; Black can use ...d5, ...Ne7-g6 or queenside space according to timing.
white_plans: Prepare d4 with pieces supporting the resulting open files.
Use Nf1-g3 and h3 to improve the kingside without weakening e4.
black_plans: Choose ...d5 when exchanges free the c8-bishop and do not lose e5.
Use ...a6/...Ba7 to preserve the bishop and prepare ...b5.

lines.name: Center Attack
lines.line: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Bc5 4. c3 Nf6 5. d4 exd4 6. cxd4 Bb4+ 7. Bd2 Bxd2+ 8. Nbxd2 d5
lines.result: The centre opens and Black uses ...d5 before White can consolidate an ideal pawn duo. Exchanges reduce attacking pieces but leave active central play.
white_plans: Use e5 only when the f6-knight has a poor square.
Bring a rook to e1 and recover any isolated pawn with activity.
black_plans: Counter in the centre rather than defend f7 passively.
Exploit checks and pins to complete development with tempo.

lines.name: Evans Gambit Accepted
lines.line: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Bc5 4. b4 Bxb4 5. c3 Ba5 6. d4 exd4 7. O-O dxc3 8. Qb3 Qf6 9. e5 Qg6 10. Nxc3
lines.result: White has restored a strong centre and a large development lead; Black has an extra pawn but the king and queenside pieces remain undeveloped.
white_plans: Use open files and development before trying to recover material.
Bring a rook to e1 and exploit the queen's awkward placement.
black_plans: Return material if it completes development or trades queens.
Avoid another queen move unless it neutralises a direct threat.

lines.name: Two Knights: quiet system
lines.line: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Nf6 4. d3 Bc5 5. O-O d6 6. c3 O-O 7. Re1 a6 8. Bb3 h6
lines.result: The game has transposed to a Pianissimo-style structure, but Black's knight reached f6 before the bishop choice.
white_plans: Use Nbd2-f1-g3 and prepare d4.
Keep the c4-bishop from being caught by ...Na5.
black_plans: Prepare ...Ba7 and ...Re8 before choosing ...d5.
Use ...a6/...b5 for space only when the centre is stable.

lines.name: Two Knights: 4.Ng5 main test
lines.line: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Nf6 4. Ng5 d5 5. exd5 Na5 6. Bb5+ c6 7. dxc6 bxc6 8. Be2 h6 9. Nf3 e4 10. Ne5
lines.result: Black has damaged queenside pawns but a strong initiative and central space; White has won a pawn and must solve the displaced knight and undeveloped queenside.
white_plans: Complete development and challenge e4 rather than hunt more pawns.
Use d3 or d4 to undermine Black's centre.
black_plans: Exploit the lead in development and open b-/d-files.
Keep e4 supported while activating the bishops.

lines.name: Hungarian Defense
lines.line: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Be7 4. d4 d6 5. Nc3 Nf6 6. O-O O-O
lines.result: Black is safe but less active than in ...Bc5 systems; White has more central room and must choose whether to clarify d4/e5.
white_plans: Use d5 only if it gains space without releasing c5.
Develop the dark bishop before launching kingside play.
black_plans: Challenge the centre with ...exd4 or ...Bg4.
Re-route the passive e7-bishop after the centre changes.

lines.name: Blackburne Shilling sideline
lines.line: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Nd4 4. Nxd4 exd4 5. O-O
lines.result: White declines the familiar e5-pawn trap by exchanging the advanced knight. Black has central space but no tactical attack on g2/e4.
white_plans: Finish development and attack d4 with c3.
Do not grab e5 without calculating ...Qg5.
black_plans: Support or exchange d4 before it becomes a target.
Develop rather than forcing a trap that is no longer present.

lines.name: Evans Gambit Declined
lines.line: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Bc5 4. b4 Bb6 5. a4 a6 6. Nc3 Nf6
lines.result: White owns queenside space but did not gain the open lines of an accepted Evans; Black keeps material equal and a sound centre.
white_plans: Use b5 carefully to displace c6 only when it does not weaken c4.
Return attention to central development with d3 or O-O.
black_plans: Counter in the centre before White's space becomes useful.
Preserve the bishop's diagonal while preparing ...d6.

transpositions.label: Pianissimo move-order
transpositions.line: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Bc5 4. d3 Nf6 5. c3
transpositions.note: The same c3/d3 structure can arise with 4.c3 Nf6 5.d3. Move order changes whether White keeps the immediate d4 option.

transpositions.label: Bishop's Opening route
transpositions.note: This reaches the Italian defining position without committing the knight on move two.

queens-gambit.title: Queen's Gambit family overview
queens-gambit.summary: White attacks the d5-pawn with a wing pawn, offering c4 only temporarily to divert Black's centre. Black's reply determines whether the struggle centres on holding d5, surrendering it for free development, or counter-gambiting against d4.
strategic_contest: White wants to remove or overload d5, then use the resulting central majority or open c-file. The c-pawn offer is usually a lever, not a permanent pawn sacrifice.
Black can support d5 with ...e6 or ...c6, accept with ...dxc4 and attack White's future centre, or challenge immediately with ...c5/...e5/...Nc6.

Recurring structures include the Carlsbad minority attack after cxd5 exd5, an isolated queen's pawn after central exchanges, and Slav structures where Black's light bishop remains outside the pawn chain.
structures: QGD structures with ...e6 secure d5 but restrict the c8-bishop; Black seeks ...c5 or ...e5 to solve the centre.
QGA structures give up d5 so Black can develop freely and later pressure White's d4/e4 centre, often accepting an isolated d-pawn as the strategic target.
Slav structures use ...c6 to support d5 without blocking the light bishop, but the c6-pawn temporarily occupies the knight's best square and slows ...c5.

decisions.title: Black chooses the central structure
decisions.why_here: Every major reply answers a different question: reinforce d5, release it, or counterattack White's centre immediately.

options.label: Queen's Gambit Declined
options.explanation: Black holds d5 with a second pawn and prepares ...Nf6. The cost is closing the c8-bishop, so the freeing ...c5 or ...e5 break becomes a long-term priority.
options.changes: Keeps central tension and invites Carlsbad, Orthodox, Tarrasch and related structures.

options.label: Queen's Gambit Accepted
options.explanation: Black abandons d5, gains a temporary pawn and develops without blocking the light bishop. Trying to keep c4 at all costs is usually less important than striking at White's centre.
options.changes: Creates an open centre and often an isolated d-pawn after White builds e4/d4.

options.label: Slav Defense
options.explanation: Black supports d5 while preserving the c8-bishop's diagonal. In return, the c6-pawn delays ...c5 and takes the c6 square from the knight.
options.changes: Produces a sound centre with different bishop-development questions from the QGD.

options.label: Albin Countergambit
options.explanation: Black answers a wing-pawn offer with a central pawn offer, seeking a cramping pawn on d4 and rapid piece activity.
options.changes: Turns a positional lever into a forcing gambit where White must challenge the advanced d4-pawn.

options.label: Chigorin Defense
options.explanation: Black develops a piece to support e5 rather than reinforcing d5 with a pawn. The knight blocks the c-pawn but encourages immediate piece play.
options.changes: Trades structural orthodoxy for active pieces and tactical central pressure.

decisions.title: White selects a QGD plan
decisions.why_here: White can develop into the main QGD, clarify the pawn structure immediately, or steer toward Catalan pressure.

options.label: Main-line pressure on d5
options.explanation: Nc3 increases pressure on d5 and supports e4, but exposes the knight to pins in Ragozin and Cambridge Springs systems.
options.changes: Keeps cxd5 flexible and permits both Orthodox and Tarrasch structures.

options.label: Flexible development
options.explanation: Nf3 avoids committing the b1-knight and can transpose to main lines or Catalan setups. It also limits an immediate e4 expansion.
options.changes: Hides White's structural choice and reduces some ...Bb4 pin ideas.

options.label: Exchange structure now
options.explanation: After ...exd5, White gets the Carlsbad structure and can plan a minority attack with b4-b5 or central e4 expansion.
options.changes: Releases central tension early and replaces opening tactics with a known asymmetric pawn plan.

options.label: Catalan direction
options.explanation: White prepares Bg2 to pressure d5/c6 from the long diagonal, often transposing to a Catalan after Nf3.
options.changes: Prioritises long-term light-square pressure over immediate occupation of e4.

decisions.title: Black answers the pin
decisions.position: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Bg5
decisions.why_here: White has tied the f6-knight to the queen; Black decides whether to break the pin, counter-pin c3, or prepare a tactical ...Qa5 system.

options.label: Orthodox development
options.explanation: Black calmly breaks the pin and prepares castling. The c8-bishop remains the strategic problem, usually solved by ...b6/...Bb7 or a freeing ...c5.
options.changes: Leads to classical QGD positions with gradual manoeuvring.

options.label: Cambridge Springs route
options.explanation: Black supports f6 and prepares ...c6 and ...Qa5, creating pressure on c3 and tactical ideas against the pinned pieces.
options.changes: Keeps the pin but introduces concrete queenside tactics.

options.label: Ragozin counter-pin
options.explanation: Black pins the c3-knight and increases control of e4. White must decide whether to play e3, Qa4+ or exchange on d5.
options.changes: Combines Nimzo-Indian piece pressure with a QGD pawn centre.

decisions.title: White builds against the accepted pawn
decisions.why_here: White can recover calmly or establish a broad centre, accepting that Black will attack it later.

options.label: Seize the full centre
options.explanation: White uses the time Black spent taking c4 to build e4/d4. Black responds with ...e5 or ...c5, trying to make that centre an object of attack.
options.changes: Creates maximum space and the greatest risk of an isolated or hanging centre.

options.label: Develop before recovery
options.explanation: White prevents ...e5 from arriving without preparation and plans e3/Bxc4. The move keeps the central pawn structure less committed.
options.changes: Favors a positional QGA where material is recovered after development.

options.label: Recover c4 directly
options.explanation: White opens the f1-bishop and threatens Bxc4. Black can use the tempo for ...e5 or ...Nf6 rather than trying to defend the extra pawn with ...b5.
options.changes: Restores material quickly but reveals White's bishop placement.

lines.name: QGD Orthodox development
lines.line: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Bg5 Be7 5. e3 O-O 6. Nf3 Nbd7 7. Rc1 c6 8. Bd3 dxc4 9. Bxc4
lines.result: White has active pieces and pressure on the centre; Black is solid and prepares ...b6/...Bb7 or ...Nd5 before the freeing ...c5.
white_plans: Use e4 only when d4 remains adequately defended.
Place rooks on c1/d1 and exploit the space advantage.
black_plans: Solve the c8-bishop with ...b6/...Bb7 or ...Nd5.
Time ...c5 so an isolated pawn is active rather than weak.

lines.name: Exchange QGD: Carlsbad structure
lines.line: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. cxd5 exd5 5. Bg5 Be7 6. e3 O-O 7. Bd3 Nbd7 8. Qc2 c6 9. Nge2 Re8 10. O-O
lines.result: The pawn structure is fixed: White can use a queenside minority attack or central e4; Black seeks kingside activity or ...Ne4 and piece play against the minority pawns.
white_plans: Prepare b4-b5 to create a target on c6.
Choose e4 when pieces can support the isolated pawn or central attack.
black_plans: Use ...Ne4 and piece activity before the minority attack lands.
Counter on the kingside or open the e-file against e3.

lines.name: Tarrasch Defense
lines.line: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 c5 4. cxd5 exd5 5. Nf3 Nc6 6. g3 Nf6 7. Bg2 Be7 8. O-O O-O
lines.result: Black accepts the prospect of an isolated d-pawn for free piece development and active central files; White tries to blockade without becoming passive.
white_plans: Pressure d5 with Bg2, Nc3 and rooks, but watch for ...d4 breaks.
Trade active pieces only when the resulting blockade is stable.
black_plans: Use activity and ...d4 before the isolani becomes a static weakness.
Place rooks on open central files and avoid unnecessary simplification.

lines.name: Queen's Gambit Accepted: 3.e4
lines.line: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 dxc4 3. e4 e5 4. Nf3 exd4 5. Bxc4 Nc6 6. O-O Be6
lines.result: White has recovered c4 and leads in development, but the d4-pawn has been exchanged and Black can challenge the remaining centre directly.
white_plans: Use development and open files rather than trying to preserve every central pawn.
Meet ...Bxc4 or ...Qd7 with quick rook development.
black_plans: Exchange White's active bishop and complete development.
Pressure e4/d4 so White's space does not become a lasting advantage.

lines.name: Main Slav structure
lines.line: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 c6 3. Nf3 Nf6 4. Nc3 dxc4 5. a4 Bf5 6. e3 e6 7. Bxc4 Bb4
lines.result: Black has developed the light bishop outside the pawn chain and returned c4; White has regained the pawn but spent a4 to prevent ...b5.
white_plans: Use Qe2/e4 when the pin on c3 is resolved.
Exploit the a4 space without weakening b4.
black_plans: Complete development and strike with ...c5.
Use the pin on c3 to control e4.

lines.name: Albin Countergambit
lines.line: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e5 3. dxe5 d4 4. Nf3 Nc6 5. a3 Be6 6. Nbd2 Qe7 7. b4 O-O-O
lines.result: Black's d4-pawn cramps White and supports practical activity, but White remains a sound pawn up if the blockade is completed. A Stockfish 19 depth-12 check strongly favoured White here, so this is presented as a response to prepare for, not as an equalising recommendation for Black.
white_plans: Blockade d4 before trying to keep the extra pawn.
Develop the queenside carefully because Black may castle long.
black_plans: Use ...Nxe5 or ...f6 to recover e5 and open lines.
Keep d4 supported only while it restricts White's pieces.

lines.name: Chigorin Defense
lines.line: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 Nc6 3. Nf3 Bg4 4. cxd5 Bxf3 5. gxf3 Qxd5 6. e3
lines.result: Black has traded a bishop to damage White's kingside pawns and activate the queen; White owns the bishop pair and central space.
white_plans: Use the bishop pair and central pawns before the structure becomes a target.
Develop with Nc3 while controlling queen checks.
black_plans: Attack d4 and exploit weakened dark squares.
Use rapid development to justify giving up the bishop pair.

lines.name: Marshall Defense
lines.line: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 Nf6 3. cxd5 Nxd5 4. e4 Nb6 5. Nf3 e5 6. Nxe5
lines.result: White has built the centre with tempo and can accept Black's attempted liquidation. A Stockfish 19 depth-12 check strongly favoured White here; the line illustrates why 2...Nf6 demands an accurate central response rather than offering Black a sound main system.
white_plans: Use the central pawns and development lead rather than chase the knight repeatedly.
Check tactics on b5 and f7 before holding extra material.
black_plans: Break the centre before White consolidates.
Develop rapidly; the moved knight must not become a permanent loss of time.

transpositions.label: Catalan route
transpositions.note: This can reach Catalan positions normally introduced through 1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 e6 3.g3 d5.

transpositions.label: Semi-Slav route
transpositions.line: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 c6 3. Nf3 Nf6 4. Nc3 e6
transpositions.note: The Slav move order transposes into a Semi-Slav once ...e6 is added; both Queen's Gambit and Slav family names remain relevant.

transpositions.label: Tarrasch by immediate ...c5
transpositions.note: The defining position may also arise through other queen-pawn move orders; classification should follow the position, not only the order.
